title: Students set new records for A-level grades in bumper year

paragraphs.en: Sixth-formers have basked in a summer of record-breaking exam results in academic and vocational subjects, allowing more than a quarter of a million 18-year-olds to go on to higher education.

The proportion of students in England gaining the highest grade of A* in A-level subjects rose to 9.7%, up from 9.4% last year, setting a new record outside the pandemic era, when exams were scrapped.
Northern Ireland was the best-performing country, with 30.7% of grades being As and A*s, followed by 29.6% in Wales and 28.7% in England.

The A-level results followed last week’s improved results in Scotland, where the proportion of students awarded Highers and Advanced Highers qualifications rose above 2019 pre-pandemic levels, and a record 18,000 Scottish school-leavers gained higher education places.

The bumper crop of results means nearly 263,000 UK pupils have already been accepted on to university courses starting this autumn, driven in part by the rising number of 18-year-olds in the population.
The results were boosted by improved results across the board, but mathematics in particular showed a strong improvement despite a rise in the number of candidates taking the subject.
Among the most striking trends this year was the surge in popularity of economics, which jumped from 10th most popular position last year to fifth, with more than 47,000 exam entries.

Myles McGinley, the managing director of the Cambridge OCR exam board, speaking at a briefing by the Joint Council for Qualifications (JCQ), said: “The students getting their A-level results today were born around 2008.
